title: The Glories of My Maker God
description: The Glories of My Maker God in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 71, headed “Praise to God from all creatures”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The glo-ries of my Mak-er God, My joy-ful voice shall sing, And call the na-tions to a-dore Their For-mer and their King.

lines: The glories of my Maker God,
And call the nations to adore
'Twas his right-hand that shap'd our clay,
But from his own immediate breath
We bring our mortal powers to God,
We claim some kindred with the skies
Let groveling beasts of every shape,
And rocks, and trees, and fires, and seas,
Ye planets, to his honour shine,
Praise him in your unwearied course
The brightness of our Maker's Name

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
